subject: general
question: Which one of the following hypotheses/theories explains the formation of the solar system from a rotating cloud of gas and dust?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Nebular Hypothesis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Nebular Hypothesis** explains the formation of the solar system from a **rotating cloud of gas and dust**, also known as a nebula.
 
• This hypothesis was first proposed by the German philosopher **Immanuel Kant** in 1755 and later expanded upon by the French mathematician **Pierre-Simon Laplace** in 1796.
 
• According to this theory, the solar system began as a giant rotating cloud of interstellar gas and dust, which began to collapse under its own gravity.
 
• As the cloud contracted, it spun faster, forming a flattened disk with the Sun forming at its center and the planets forming from the remaining matter in the disk.
 
• This hypothesis remains one of the most widely accepted explanations for the formation of the solar system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Big Bang Theory:**

 
 
• The Big Bang Theory describes the origin of the **universe**, not the formation of the solar system.
 
• It proposes that the universe began as a singularity approximately **13.8 billion years ago** and has been expanding ever since.
 
 
 
• **Continental Drift Theory:**
 
 
• This theory, proposed by **Alfred Wegener** in 1912, explains the movement of Earth's **continental plates** over geological time.
 
• It is unrelated to the formation of the solar system and instead pertains to the Earth's lithosphere.
 
 
 
• **Plate Tectonics Theory:**
 
 
• Plate Tectonics Theory explains the movement of Earth's lithospheric plates and the resulting geological phenomena, such as **earthquakes** and **volcanic activity**.
 
• It is distinct from the Nebular Hypothesis and is focused on the geological processes of Earth.
 
 
 
• **Formation of Planets:**
 
 
• According to the Nebular Hypothesis, planets formed through a process called **accretion**, where dust and gas particles collided and stuck together to form larger bodies.
 
• The inner planets (Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars) are rocky due to high temperatures near the Sun, while the outer planets (Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune) are gaseous and icy.
 
 
 
• **Modern Support:**
 
 
• Modern observations, such as the discovery of **protoplanetary disks** around young stars and the study of meteorites, provide strong evidence for the Nebular Hypothesis.
 
• Space missions like NASA's **Kepler** and **James Webb Space Telescope** have further validated elements of this theory.
